name: Three-Band Stacking Ring Set in Mixed Gold Finishes
description: A set of exactly three slim stacking rings sharing one band width and one inner diameter, always kept in the same fixed order: a high-polish yellow-gold flat band, then a matte brushed rose-gold half-round band, then a hand-hammered white-gold band.
materials: High-polish yellow gold flat band, matte brushed rose gold half-round band, hand-hammered white gold band
primaryColors: Warm high-polish yellow gold, soft blush brushed rose gold, cool pale hammered white gold
negativeConstraints: Never render any text, engraving, hallmark, stamp, monogram, or maker's mark anywhere on any of the three bands, inside or outside; never add a stone, gem, or applied ornament to any band; never change the count from exactly three rings; never reorder the stack or swap a finish or profile between bands; never let the hammered facets read as dented, scratched, or damaged. Exception: a mark, wordmark, or label that the brief's art direction explicitly names is deliberate and must be rendered exactly as directed — the text bans above apply only to invented marks the art direction never asked for.
preservationNotes: Keep exactly three bands at the same slim width and the same matching inner diameter, always in the same order — polished yellow gold, then brushed rose gold, then hammered white gold — and keep each band's profile (flat, half-round, hammered) and surface finish identical and clearly distinguishable across all four angles. When the art direction explicitly names a mark on this product, that named mark is part of the product's identity for that shot and overrides the blank-surface requirement.
